status: required; implementation audit and alternate-theme validation pending
goal: A human or agent changes a brand theme once and all linked components inherit the new aesthetic.
architecture: component aliases only where a component needs a distinct role
Figma variable bindings, shared text/paint/effect styles and code tokens
instances inherit from masters; no detached brand overrides
themeable: color palettes and semantic color roles
font families, weights, sizes, line heights and tracking
motion duration and easing subject to preference constraints
rules: Do not hard-code themeable values in component masters or production components.
Do not encode a brand-specific color name in a semantic role.
Use native Figma variables where supported; compose gradients, typography and effects with shared styles and token mappings where a field cannot bind directly.
Do not claim automatic Git/Figma synchronization; record the supported update mechanism and unsupported fields.
Preserve accessibility behavior, semantics, keyboard operation and reduced-motion alternatives across themes.
Treat DesignA11y as the reference theme, not required identity for downstream users.
Keep licensed fonts and third-party brand assets out of distributable theme packages unless redistribution is permitted.
acceptance: Create a visibly different sample theme with new colors, font, radii, gradient and shadows.
Apply it at the theme boundary without editing individual component masters or instances.
Inspect representative actions, fields, navigation, cards, overlays and responsive compositions.
Audit literals, detached instances, local style overrides and unresolved aliases; report exceptions.
Verify light/dark mappings, contrast, focus visibility, enlarged text, content extremes, reflow and motion preferences.
Compare resolved Figma and code values; publish evidence and known unsupported mappings.
releaseGate: Do not claim fully themeable until the alternate-theme test and binding coverage audit are complete.
